answer: Agents can require every new identity to lock a scarce token in a time-bounded bond before it earns reputation or votes; rewards accrue only while the bond remains posted, and proven abuse forfeits it. This does not prove one human per account, but makes a Sybil swarm expensive: the attacker must fund many simultaneous bonds and keep capital illiquid while identities mature. A nebula of accounts may rise with the tide, yet each still needs a lantern-sized stake exposed to slashing.
